emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep smuggling instructions into autonomous AI agents through untrusted content, with Ghostcommit hiding a prompt injection inside a PNG image and HalluSquatting exploiting model hallucinations to deliver remote code.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hidden Prompt Injection Hijacks AI Agents

emerging_trends.text: American courts are turning on the ransomware ecosystem's enablers, sentencing a former BlackCat negotiator to 70 months and accepting a Ryuk operator's guilty plea.
Defenders are racing broad campaigns hunting internet-facing software, as Australia warns of mass content management system exploitation while CISA flags actively abused Joomla extensions.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Mass Exploitation of CMS and Git Platforms

topics.title: Mass Exploitation of CMS and Git Platforms
topics.latest_developments: The Australian Cyber Security Centre warned July 11, 2026 of a global campaign hitting vulnerable content management systems and plugins, the same week CISA added two actively exploited Joomla extension file-upload flaws—iCagenda's CVE-2026-48939 and Balbooa Forms' CVE-2026-56291—to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and attackers began abusing an authentication-bypass bug in the official Gitea Docker image to impersonate administrators.
topics.summary: The campaigns target internet-facing web software—content management systems such as Joomla, their extensions, and self-hosted Git services; operators should patch immediately and inspect for unauthorized accounts and web shells.

sources.title: Australia warns of global campaign targeting vulnerable CMS platforms
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Hackers exploit critical auth bypass in Gitea Docker image

topics.title: Hidden Prompt Injection Hijacks AI Agents
topics.latest_developments: Researchers demonstrated Ghostcommit on July 11, 2026, a prompt injection concealed inside a PNG image that slipped past the CodeRabbit and Bugbot AI code reviewers—which never open image files—and coaxed a coding agent into reading a repository's .env file and writing every secret back as a list of numbers, as SecurityWeek detailed HalluSquatting, which exploits AI-assistant hallucinations to reach remote code execution and seed a botnet, and The Hacker News mapped a WhatsApp-to-host chain through three flaws in the OpenClaw personal AI assistant.
topics.summary: The attacks target autonomous AI agents and assistants that read untrusted content; teams deploying coding agents should treat every model input as hostile and restrict what secrets and hosts an agent can reach.

sources.title: 'Ghostcommit' hides prompt injection in images to fool AI agents, steal secrets
‘HalluSquatting’ Turns AI Hallucinations Into Botnet Delivery Mechanism
Researcher Details WhatsApp-to-Host Attack Chain Using Three OpenClaw Flaws

topics.title: Critical Zimbra Web Client Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Zimbra urged customers on July 10, 2026 to patch a critical stored cross-site-scripting flaw in the Classic Web Client of Zimbra Collaboration that lets a crafted email run arbitrary scripts in a victim's session; the bug carries no CVE identifier yet.
topics.summary: Zimbra Collaboration is a widely deployed email and groupware suite, and administrators running the Classic Web Client should apply the fix now, since exploitation needs only a malicious email a user opens.

sources.title: Critical Zimbra Flaw Could Let Crafted Emails Run Malicious Code in User Sessions
Zimbra urges customers to patch critical web client XSS flaw

topics.title: Ransomware Operators and Enablers Sentenced
topics.latest_developments: A 34-year-old Armenian man pleaded guilty in an Oregon federal court to conspiracy and computer fraud for deploying Ryuk ransomware against US companies and now faces up to 15 years, while Angelo Martino, 41, a former DigitalMint ransomware negotiator, drew 70 months in a Florida federal court for secretly helping the BlackCat/AlphV gang extort victims in 2023, the third US security professional imprisoned in that scheme.
topics.summary: Ryuk and BlackCat/AlphV rank among the most damaging ransomware operations, and the sentencings show US prosecutors reaching both foreign operators and the American incident-response insiders who turned on their own clients.

sources.title: Ryuk operator pleads guilty; Blackcat/AlphV conspirator gets nearly 6-year sentence
Ryuk ransomware member pleads guilty in the US, faces 15 years in prison
Third US Security Expert Sentenced to Prison for Helping Ransomware Gang

topics.title: Progress ShareFile Emergency Shutdown
topics.latest_developments: Progress Software emailed ShareFile customers on July 10, 2026 to immediately power off the Windows servers running their on-premises Storage Zone Controllers and disabled access to affected accounts, citing a credible external security threat it is still investigating with outside responders.
topics.summary: ShareFile is Progress's enterprise secure file-sharing platform, and the Storage Zone Controllers hold customer data on-premises; administrators who run them should shut the servers down and watch for further guidance from Progress.

sources.title: URGENT - Progress Tells ShareFile Customers to Shut Down Storage Zone Controllers Over Security Threat
Progress urges ShareFile admins to shut down servers over “credible” threat

topics.title: EU Parliament Passes Chat Control 2.0
topics.latest_developments: The European Parliament passed the law known as Chat Control 2.0 on July 10, 2026, permitting companies including Google, Meta, and Microsoft to scan users' private messages in search of child sexual abuse material.
topics.summary: Chat Control 2.0 revives a contested EU proposal that sets child-safety scanning against end-to-end encryption and message privacy, and providers operating in the EU now must weigh how to scan content while preserving their encryption guarantees.

sources.title: Europe revives law allowing big tech to scan for CSAM
